It is quite clear, the situation was quite clear in Podrinje in 1992, at the time, when there was a polarisation in the achievement of the interests of individual peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Podrinje and other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina, where the Serb people lived or were a majority, were cut in several parts, and it was this other side that advocated a unitary Bosnia-Herzegovina as internationally recognised. Podrinje was cut in several parts. And at one point in time quite simply the Serb people in the area of the municipality of Bratunac was in such a position that they could not function or, rather, the state could not function and communications could not function, roads, electronic communications, so people lived there and -- actually, in part of my statement I said that in -- that on the 8th of January, 1993, our group tried to get to Han Pijesak and we had an armed escort and we weren't even taking the main roads but we took various paths via Vlasenica and that's how we arrived at Han Pijesak and some people who were supposed to get to Herzegovina were sent via Zvornik to Serbia and then they arrived via Trebinje into Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that I wanted to prevent terrorist activities from the enclave and consolidate the lines of the Army of Republika Srpska around the enclaves. Can you explain this to the Trial Chamber, what your understanding was of that and whether that was in the context of our conversation when I asked you for advice?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It so happened because of my position and the location where the meeting took place, when Saint Vitus' Day was being commemorated at Mount Romanija where I was brigade commander. I was in position to host the event in a way -- or, rather, to be the host of the head of the Main Staff and you, as the Supreme Commander. However metropolitan Nikolai and other church dignitaries later on after the event and after the decorations ceremony and after reminiscing about struggles before 1995, a memorial room was supposed to be opened dedicated to the memory of the killed soldiers from the municipality of Sokolac. As we walked towards that room I happened to be next to you, and you asked me about my position about that. You asked me what I thought about that, setting up a single operative command for the area of the enclaves. In view of the activities of sabotage groups around the villages that were around the enclaves, through the lines, check-points, observation points of the United Nations, in April and June 1995, there were several incursions of this nature, and that resulted in the decision on the order for active efforts, and although this order was already in existence, you were still thinking about how this should be done, whether this command should be established as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now the Prosecution may continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic. Mr. Trivic, as you have noted, your evidence-in-chief in this case has been admitted in its most part in writing, that is through your written statement in lieu of your oral testimony. And now you'll be cross-examined by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pack.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Colonel Trivic, let's start with 1995. This is when you were brigade commander of the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Now, you've just been speaking about a meeting which you apparently had with Dr. Karadzic in the last week of June 1995, is that approximately when you say it was?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In my statement it is more precise than in the summary that was presented by Mr. Karadzic. It was Sunday, not a week. It was the Sunday after Saint Vitus' Day. I don't know exactly what the date was, but Saint Vitus' Day is on the 28th of June, as is well known.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: So the 28th of June in 1995, if it fell on a Wednesday that would have been the 2nd of July, the Sunday?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: 2nd, 3rd, I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And that's the date upon which was issued the preparatory order to which you have referred in your -- in your statement, yes?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the date when the preparatory order was issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Is the preparatory order which I'm not going to show you, you have seen it on numerous occasions when you testified here. It's P04571, Your Honours. This is the order that describes what was needed to be done to prepare units for Krivaja 95; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Now, this preparatory order of course related -- was issued pursuant to Directives 7, 7/1. You remember that from your prior testimony, don't you? Yes?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Whether it has to do with Directive 7 or 7/1, I would like to see the first page of the order, if you could please display it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Due to technical difficulties, we will pause for two or three minutes. Shall we test whether it's working now? Very well. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You wanted to see the order. It's up on the screen. Just please look at -- in the B/C/S, fourth paragraph down, you can see, please, it's paragraph 2, the command of the Drina Corps pursuant to operations directive number 7, and 7/1 of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, and so on. So that's the preparatory order. You'd accept it was issued pursuant to those two directives, yes?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: First of all, I'd like to say that this preparatory order was issued due to the reason stated under item 1. Item 2 represents and makes reference to the authority on the basis of which the corps command is going to implement these activities. Therefore, under item 1 the corps command cites the reasons on the basis of which it is undertaking certain activities, and then under item 2, it invokes the principle that it is authorised to carry out that because the directive for that year was something that pointed to active operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Colonel Trivic was that a long way of saying yes, this preparatory order was issued pursuant to operations directive number 7, and 7/1 as it says there at paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can we go to Directive 7, it's P00838. I'd like to remind you of a paragraph you've looked at numerous times before. It's page 10 in the English, B/C/S page 15. You of course remember testifying previously in the Popovic case that the Supreme Commander is responsible for this document as the signatory; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to listen to and to know exactly what I said. The responsibility for every document lies with those who signed it, but he is also authorising and issuing guidelines to everybody who is involved and who is nominated in the document itself, and as far as that goes, I agree with you, I don't understand why you use the word "responsible." It is beyond doubt that the person who signs the document stands behind everything contained in that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you, could we look at page 10, please, the last -- the last sentence, please, in the bottom paragraph of the -- of the English and of course in the B/C/S the equivalent, at page 15. You're familiar with it by now. The sentence which reads: "By planned and well thought out combat operations create an unbearable situation of total insecurity with no hope of further survival or life for the inhabitants of Srebrenica and Zepa." Now, I'd like to remind you of your prior testimony in the Mladic case. You testified in the Mladic case a few weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 25276, please, Mr. President, and I'd like to look, please, at -- have on the screen and I'll read out page 120 of e-court. 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: 120 just has questions from the judge and -- and your -- your response is in fact at page 121 of e-court if we could just turn over. Just to provide you the context, the questions were about this sentence. And you responded at line 20 of page 121 in e-court, you responded as follows, I'll read it slowly: "This sentence, Mr. President, this sentence was uttered in a somewhat different way as compared to the terminology that is used by forces that are preparing to topple regimes in different parts of the world. These are sanctions, just phrased differently." And then the judge goes -- the judge says: "But is that your interpretation of the document? Where does it come from that you say this is what was meant despite the clear language of the document?" And then you respond: "Well, I haven't received this document but I believe it is my understanding of this that these different activities through combat activities and through narrowing the area of the enclaves and interrupting communication between the two enclaves the population should have a growing awareness of them being, in a way, prisoners of their own leaders and that therefore these leaders should be changed." Remember that testimony in the Mladic case?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Do you stand by that evidence? You stand by that evidence, that the aim of this -- this sentence here in Directive 7, "create an unbearable situation of total insecurity with no hope of further survival or life," that may be compared to the imposition by a state or states of sanctions?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: I stand by what I said, but the first part of the question, although we don't have it in the Serbian which I would have preferred so that I can prove to you, at the beginning of my answer, I received an interpretation something like a sentence uttered, et cetera. This sentence had not been uttered. This sentence defines or, rather, provides guidelines to the activities in 1993, the activities that would lead to such a situation in which the inhabitants of the enclave would undertake certain measures to participate in a way in having the regime who is doing wrongful things and therefore making the population suffer be changed and that the enclaves --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last part of his answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Trivic, could you repeat your last answer, the last part of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that in that sense, I stand by my view that the activities in 1993, not in one month or in one day alone, require the change of the political leadership, whose escapades were putting them, themselves, in a hopeless situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You're talking about 1995; right? This document is dated 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, I said 1993. My mistake. It should be 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You'd accept that these are very grave words, wouldn't you, very grave words?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: These words, these words, this sentence, this aim that is expressed there, it's very grave, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: There is no objective stipulated in the directive. The directive is not a binding document. It is a document providing guidelines for certain activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let me ask you, please, to look at your prior testimony in the Mladic case again, at page 138 of e-court, just like to remind you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript, in line 21, the witness said that the directive does not have any objective and then he said the directive is not a binding document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You now have that on the screen. The bit I wanted to read out to you was this, questions from Prosecution counsel in the Mladic case about these words. He says: "Q. But these are amazing words. I won't repeat them again, 'make life unbearable for the people.' Certainly you would have remembered those words if they had been given to you from your superiors, yes or no, do you remember or not? "A. I assume I would remember. These are very grave words but let's not go into any further explanations. I assume that if they had been put that way I would have remembered, but here in this context of this directive they do not have that meaning. I explained -- I tried to explain --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please slow down while reading. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let me -- let me just take it up because I've gone too fast. I'll just repeat from: "I assume that if they had been put that way I would have remembered, but here in this context of this directive they do not have that meaning. I explained -- I tried to explain, present, well, not explain, sorry, I meant I tried to present my point of view." So I've just read all of your answer. You have identified -- you have stated there --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: My question is that you have stated there, haven't you, that these words are very grave, yes? Very grave?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC
utterances.text: If you allow me, those were not words, that was a written document. None of my superiors ever informed me verbally to act in that way. After all, an order that I have to act upon as well as other subordinate corps commands did not receive such a task.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn for today and continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. As you are well aware, Mr. Trivic, please do not discuss with anybody else about your testimony while you're giving testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 27th day of June, 2013, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
